completion_criteria.text: U1-U7 experiments run and recorded in a companion findings doc; each claim marked verified or refuted with evidence, before any step that depends on it
Step 0 shipped: protect-claude-config.sh narrowed to the gate implementation and deny list only, ask converted to deny, confirmed live
Promotion manifest hardened first: hooks and permissions.deny reclassified so absence refuses promotion rather than deleting from live, and undeclared keys are refused instead of freezing
Delivery path restored under Layer 0: GH_TOKEN exported so gh and git authenticate over HTTPS, and an agent pushes a branch and opens a PR with signed commits and no human hands
Steps 1-2 shipped: deny pruned to D1-D5 only; all ask rules retired and hook ask branches converted to checkpoint-and-allow or block
Steps 3-4 shipped: allow rules enumerate narrow command prefixes plus mcp__* coverage; settings.local.json truncated to reusable prefix rules and accumulation stopped at source
Layer 1 shipped whole: per-worktree temp-index checkpoint using --force, rm-to-trash rewrite, hourly APFS snapshot, and the D2 age-based reaper in the same change
Layer 3 shipped: one PreToolUse gate, P0-P6 in order, allow/block only, fail-open except P1/P2/P5, honoring the D3 local-container carve-out
Layer 4 shipped: append-only tool-call audit log plus a SessionStart heartbeat asserting layers 0 and 1 and the promotion pointer
Layer 0 shipped: sandbox with allowLocalBinding, allowUnsandboxedCommands false and failIfUnavailable true, keeping filesystem containment with working localhost
Steps 8-9 shipped: inert and harmful hooks deleted; logbook plugin fail-closed guard disabled or patched (R6)
R3 rule change landed: the standing --dangerously-skip-permissions prohibition replaced by a rule requiring layers 0, 1 and 4 live first
Release path closed: a staleness heartbeat reports when local main is behind the remote without applying, and a verify verb asserts installed machinery matches its tracked source
Governed unattended launcher: a version-controlled script is the sole entry point, hardcodes the permission mode, and passes through no caller settings, closing the inline-JSON argv channel
One PR per MSP opened through the centralized pr-create tool, each leaving its base branch green

spine.active_goal: Ship the amended maximum-autonomy permission architecture one PR per MSP onto docs/max-autonomy-permission-spec, holding the two oversight-reducing pieces for direct user confirmation.
spine.next_step: Base is GREEN after PR 93 merged (248 config tests, 0 fail, verified on 9dea58b). Awaiting c6 (Layer 3 gate) and c7 (Layer 4), both still running. Neither can push - gh cannot read its config from any agent process - so relay each one's branch, verification output and a ready-to-run pr-create for the user's terminal. PR 92 (Layer 1) still open. Then c3 then c4, gated behind the gate landing per 0401. c14 and the plugin disable stay HELD; no decision on 0398.
spine.last_session: Ten units built, seven merged. The composed base went red on 11 stale-fixture tests and was repaired by PR 93, which also closed two proven HIGH findings from the security review. Network egress to GitHub died mid-session; the user pushed and opened PR 93 by hand.

open_risks.text: No agent process can reach GitHub — ssh fails at nc negotiation, https gets CONNECT 403, and gh cannot read its own config; every remaining PR must be pushed and opened from the user's terminal, so hand over a ready-to-run pr-create rather than attempting it

Parallel authoring against a moving base is what reddened the branch — each PR was genuinely green alone; any future fan-out must rebase workers onto the current tip and run the full suite at the merge boundary, not only per-branch
Commits produced while network-blocked are unsigned because gnupg is unreadable from the agent sandbox — if the repo or CI ever requires signatures these need amending with git commit --amend -S

The cutover to main lands everything at once on the working machine — sandbox on with failIfUnavailable true, config guard flipping ask to deny, three hooks gone, per-action checkpointing at 122 ms; it deserves a planned cutover, not a casual merge

Eleven agent worktrees have accumulated under .claude/worktrees/agent-* with two still in use by running agents — worth one deliberate sweep after everything lands, never while agents are live in them

key_decisions.title: D2 guards the live installed copy, not version-controlled source
The D6 checkpoint runs at the worktree root and requires --force
Allow rules enumerate narrow prefixes; a broad Bash star rule is counterproductive
Layer 0 survives on one key; the default sandbox configuration is unsafe
Oversight-reducing changes wait for direct user confirmation
Default-branch push denies stay, reclassified as delivery contract not catastrophe
Merging to live stays an explicit human act with loud staleness reporting
No deny entry is removed until its replacement exists
HTTPS and GH_TOKEN are the delivery path under Layer 0

out_of_scope: Re-running any U1-U7 experiment - all seven are resolved with evidence in the findings doc, and re-running them costs hours and risks tripping the security flags that already fired twice
Pruning the 58 refs left under refs/checkpoint-experiment/ - deleting refs is trivial but reclaiming the roughly 9 MB needs gc --prune, which is guarded under D2 and is a human act
